identity.real_world_identity_notes: Customer GT4 racing car based on the F82 M4 Coupe, sold from 2018. BMW's launch material lists a 2,979 cc six-cylinder in-line M TwinPower turbo engine and a seven-gear dual clutch transmission with motorsport software, carried over from the production car rather than a bespoke racing sequential. That matches the seven forward gears exercised in the drive.

wheel_rim.notes: Observed from the cockpit during the guided drive.

notes: Simulator behavior was directly observed in a guided drive with automatic clutch and shifting disabled.
The gearbox is a production-derived seven-speed dual clutch rather than a racing sequential, which is why it has seven gears where most GT4 cars have six.
No throttle lift is required on upshifts and no manual blip on downshifts, because the drive detected automatic cut and automatic blip.
Observed live in AMS2 1.6.9.91 via guided verification observation ams2.bmw-m4-gt4.20260813t164859994z-2a3b64ae by Jason Kinslow.

confidence.basis: Simulator behavior was live-tested in AMS2 1.6.9.91 with automatic clutch and shifting disabled, and the real-world transmission is established by a registered manufacturer source.

claims.basis: The registered manufacturer source establishes the real-world identity and transmission, and the exact simulator identity was observed live.
BMW specifies a seven-gear dual clutch transmission with motorsport software; the live drive confirmed seven paddle-selected gears and clutch-free move-off.
Directly observed during the guided drive: move-off, shift clutch use, automatic cut and blip, and the cockpit rim.

notes: The wheel-rim shape was originally recorded as "gt-style". The separate "gt-style", "formula" and "prototype" values described the same rim: molded grips at 9 and 3 with a control face between them, usually carrying a display and rev lights. They are merged into "gt-formula". The rim was not observed again and nothing about the observation changed.
